correctness.rationale: The canonical formula and expected-dimension equation give the exact identity \(qB=\sum_i(d_i-1)\binom{d_i+k}{k}-(q^2+2)\), with \(q=k+1\). The lower bounds in the cases of at least three equations, two equations, one equation of degree at least three, and a single quadric establish nonnegativity and isolate equality. The two-quadric equality forces \(q=2\) and \(r=5\). The apparent boundary \(r=2k+m\) does not produce an expected surface under the stated degree constraints, so the smooth expected-surface regime is consistent. Fresh bounded replay over 3,065 valid parameter tuples corroborated the proof and found the unique zero only.

final_claim: For a general complete intersection whose \(k\)-plane Fano scheme has expected dimension two in the standard range, the canonical Plücker coefficient \(B\) is nonnegative, and \(B=0\) occurs exactly for lines on a general intersection of two quadrics in \(\mathbb P^5\); every other such surface has ample canonical bundle.
limitations: General complex complete intersections only; special fibers with excess dimension, singularities, or extra components are outside scope.
